en.tldr: This paper is the first to systematically study group-level hateful narratives in multi-turn text-to-image generation, revealing severe vulnerabilities in current models and moderation systems, and proposing interaction-aware monitoring and post-generation joint analysis defenses.
en.motivation: Existing research focuses on hateful content in single images, overlooking the group-level hateful meaning conveyed by ordered image sets in multi-turn generation, which can be cheaply and scalably produced, posing threats especially to children.
en.method: Constructed HatefulStoryPrompts with 330 multi-turn configurations from 55 hateful stories across two languages and three visual styles, evaluated five frontier models; built HatefulVisualStory dataset (969 hateful image sets and 990 benign controls) to evaluate existing moderation systems; proposed interaction-aware monitor and post-generation joint analysis defenses.
en.result: All models completed over 80% of hateful stories, with the strongest reaching 99.0%; existing moderation systems achieved at most 67.5% recall (strong VLM) and 34.9% (dedicated safety models); proposed interaction-aware monitor achieved 97.3% recall for prompt-only sessions and 92.6% when user supplies first image, while post-generation joint analysis reached 80.2%.
en.help_to_user: Helps security researchers and platform developers understand the risks of hateful narratives in multi-turn image generation and provides actionable detection and defense strategies.

idea_spark.idea: Treat multi-turn generation as a sequence and use cross-image relational reasoning to identify group-level malicious intent, rather than relying solely on individual images.
idea_spark.risk: Defenses may be bypassed by adversarial attacks, and false positives may occur on benign but sensitive narratives.
idea_spark.inspiration: Leverage narrative understanding and multimodal reasoning techniques to develop more robust stateful moderation systems.

papers.title: Challenges for Musical Education in the Age of AI and Digital Transformation
papers.summary: Music education has never been a static discipline. Each major technological shift has forced educators and institutions to reconsider what they teach, how they teach it, and why. We now stand at what may be the most consequential of such turning points. Three deeply intertwined transformations have been converging simultaneously: 1. The very nature of music has changed: how it is made, distributed, consumed, and valued; 2. The public for music has changed: listening habits are now shaped by streaming algorithms and the boundary between consumer and creator has blurred; 3. Music-making itself has changed: digital audio workstations (DAWs) have for two decades been reshaping compositional practice. In addition, generative AI has now irrupted, capable of producing complete, stylistically coherent musical pieces from a short text prompt. These changes are not independent of one another, and they all bear directly on musical education - both the content that must be taught, and the pedagogical tools and methods available to teach it. This paper attempts to map these challenges and to consider how education might adapt. Section 2 surveys the changes in various aspects of music (nature, production, public, economics). Section 3 examines the implications for education before Section 4 concludes.

ai.tldr: 本文探讨了人工智能和数字化转型对音乐教育带来的挑战，分析了音乐本质、公众、制作方式的变化及其对教学内容和方法的启示。
ai.motivation: 音乐教育历来随技术变革而调整，当前生成式AI和数字工具正深刻改变音乐创作、传播和消费，教育必须适应这些变化。
ai.method: 通过综述音乐在本质、生产、公众、经济等方面的变化，分析其对音乐教育的影响，并提出适应策略。
ai.result: 识别出音乐教育面临的多重挑战，包括教学内容更新、教学方法革新以及教育工具整合等。
ai.help_to_user: 帮助音乐教育者理解AI时代音乐教育的关键问题，为课程设计和教学改革提供参考。

idea_spark.idea: 开发结合生成式AI的互动教学平台，让学生通过提示词创作音乐并分析AI生成作品，以理解音乐结构与风格。
idea_spark.risk: 过度依赖AI可能削弱学生的基础音乐技能和创造力，需平衡技术使用与传统训练。
idea_spark.inspiration: 借鉴其他学科（如计算机科学）的AI教育方法，设计音乐教育特有的AI应用场景。

en.tldr: This paper explores the challenges that AI and digital transformation pose to music education, analyzing changes in the nature of music, its production, public, and economics, and their implications for teaching content and methods.
en.motivation: Music education has always adapted to technological shifts; the current convergence of generative AI and digital tools is transforming music creation, distribution, and consumption, necessitating educational adaptation.
en.method: A survey of changes in various aspects of music (nature, production, public, economics) and an examination of their implications for music education.
en.result: Identifies key challenges for music education, including updating curriculum content, innovating pedagogical methods, and integrating new tools.
en.help_to_user: Helps music educators understand critical issues in the age of AI and provides a basis for curriculum design and teaching reform.

idea_spark.idea: Develop an interactive teaching platform that combines generative AI, allowing students to create music via prompts and analyze AI-generated works to understand musical structure and style.
idea_spark.risk: Over-reliance on AI may weaken students' fundamental musical skills and creativity; a balance between technology and traditional training is needed.
idea_spark.inspiration: Draw from AI education methods in other disciplines (e.g., computer science) to design music-specific AI applications.
